strain of E. coli has the serC gene knocked out to prevent biosynthesis of phosphoserine, which would compete with nhpSer for incorporation into proteins ( Figure 1 ). This strain contains Release Factor 1 (RF1), the protein responsible for terminating translation at TAG amber codons, so truncated protein will be produced along with full-length nhpSer-protein. To avoid co-purification of truncated protein with full-length protein, C-terminal purification tags are recommended. For proteins that self-assemble into homo-multimers (dimers, trimers, etc.), purification can be challenging due to the possible co-purification of truncated forms that are incorporated as subunits in the assembly. If using N-terminal purification/solubilization tags, additional purifications steps may be needed to remove truncated protein species. See General note 1 for more discussion. DH10b (Thermo Fisher, catalog number: EC0113). This strain can be used for faithful propagation of plasmids and for cloning needs when users wish to clone their genes of interest into the pRBC plasmid (see Plasmids below). Do not use for protein expression. Though we have not explicitly tested all of them, other classical cloning strains of E. coli can be used including NEB 10-beta (New England BioLabs, catalog number: C3019H), DH5α (e.g., Thermo Fisher, catalog number: 18258012), NEB 5-alpha (New England BioLabs, catalog number: C2987H), or TOP10 (Thermo Fisher, catalog number: C404010). Plasmids pERM2-nhpSer (Addgene, #201922): machinery plasmid for nhpSer incorporation, kanamycin resistance with pUC origin of replication. This plasmid expresses the same tRNA synthetase and EF-Tu used for pSer incorporation ( Rogerson et al., 2015 ). The amber codon suppressing Sep-tRNA CUA is v2.0 developed by Chin and colleagues to minimize mis-aminoacylation ( Zhang et al., 2017 ). The Sep-tRNA and tRNA-synthetase are constitutively expressed via lpp and GlnS promoters, respectively. The EF-Tu is under control of an IPTG inducible tac promoter. Also constitutively expressed via an OXB20 promoter is the E. coli serB protein to further eliminate (hydrolyze) free pSer amino acid that may come from the media or produced by promiscuous transaminases. pCDF-Frb-v1 (Addgene, #201923): expresses Streptomyces rubellomurinus FrbA, FrbB, FrbC, FrbD, and FrbE enzymes required for the biosynthesis of nhpSer. See Zhu et al. (

for a detailed description of this biosynthetic pathway, which is also summarized in Figure 2 . Each Frb protein is expressed under the control of an engineered T7 transcriptional promoter variant and so all Frb enzyme are expressed by the addition of IPTG. This plasmid confers spectinomycin resistance and contains the CloDF origin of replication. This plasmid is large (~11 kb) and contains repetitive elements; while we have not observed instability of this plasmid, given its large size it is good practice to minimize propagations. We recommend that when you receive the DH10b cells with the pCDF-Frb-v1 plasmid from Addgene, grow up a few individual colonies overnight in liquid media [e.g., 2× YT media supplemented with spectinomycin at 100 μg/mL (see Recipes)] and make frozen glycerol stocks of the cells for long-term storage. Glycerol stocks can be made by mixing 600 μL of overnight culture with 400 μL of sterile 50% (v/v) glycerol. Place culture tube(s) in -80 °C freezer for storage. These stocks serve as a permanent, long-term source of plasmid, which can be prepared by inoculating cultures with cells from a glob of the frozen glycerol stock. Do not thaw the glycerol stock(s) once frozen. pRBC-sfGFP wild-type (Addgene, #174075): expresses wild-type sfGFP control protein with C-terminal His6 tag, under a T7 transcriptional promoter, ampicillin resistance/p15a origin of replication. sfGFP is expressed by the addition of IPTG. pRBC-sfGFP 150TAG (Addgene, #174076): same as above except the sfGFP gene contains a TAG amber stop codon at site N

The TAG codon is used to direct the translational encoding of nhpSer. Note that this is also the same plasmid used for pSer encoding ( Zhu et al., 2022 ); any protein cloned into this vector for pSer encoding will also work for nhpSer encoding. See General note 2 for more discussions. pRBC-[x] wild type (you must create): expresses your wild-type protein of interest (POI). You can clone your POI into pRBC by removing the sfGFP gene from the pRBC-sfGFP wt plasmid by restriction digest with NdeI and XhoI enzymes and replacing it with your POI gene using standard cloning techniques (e.g., ligation, Gibson Assembly, or SLiCE). For reasons mentioned above, a C-terminal purification tag is preferred. For helpful tips on construct design, see Troubleshooting

pRBC-[x] TAG (you must create): expresses your POI with nhpSer encoded at a TAG codon. You can clone your POI into pRBC by removing the sfGFP gene by restriction digest with NdeI and XhoI and replacing with your POI gene using standard cloning techniques (e.g., ligation, Gibson Assembly, or SLiCE). steps.title: Prepare LB agar plate and streak cells
steps.instruction: Prepare a LB/agar plate (no antibiotics), allow it to cool to room temperature until solidified. Streak BL21(DE3) ΔserC cells from a frozen glycerol stock onto the plate, place the plate upside‑down in a static 37 °C incubator and grow overnight (14–20 h).

steps.title: Refrigerate plate and prepare media
steps.instruction: Refrigerate the overnight LB/agar plate for the remainder of the day. Autoclave 1 L of 2× YT media in a 2.8 L baffled Fernbach flask. Prepare 1 L of 10 % (v/v) glycerol solution, autoclave it together with a 500 mL graduated cylinder, two 0.5 L centrifuge bottles, a box of 1 000 µL, 100 µL and 10 µL pipette tips, and ~50 × 0.6 mL Eppendorf tubes. After autoclaving, chill the glycerol solution overnight in a refrigerator or cold room.

steps.title: Inoculate starter culture overnight
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL sterile 2× YT media to a 14 mL culture tube, inoculate with a single colony from the refrigerated LB/agar plate, and grow overnight at 37 °C with shaking at 250 rpm.

steps.title: Scale up culture to 1 L and grow to OD0.4
steps.instruction: Inoculate 1 L 2× YT (in a 2.8 L baffled Fernbach flask) with the 5 mL overnight starter culture, add ~5–6 drops of antifoam, and grow at 37 °C, 200–250 rpm until OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.4 (≈ 2–3 h). Do not let OD exceed 0.5. Pre‑chill the centrifuge, rotor, bottles and graduated cylinder to 4 °C.

steps.title: Cold‑shock and harvest cells
steps.instruction: Place the 1 L culture in an ice/water bath for 15 min, mixing occasionally. Transfer the chilled culture into two pre‑chilled 0.5 L centrifuge bottles and centrifuge at 4 000 × g, 15 min, 4 °C. Discard supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Wash cells with cold glycerol (multiple rounds)
steps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in 250 mL ice‑cold 10 % (v/v) glycerol by gentle swirling (no vortex). Combine the two resuspensions into one 0.5 L bottle, centrifuge again at 4 000 × g, 15 min, 4 °C. Discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in another 250 mL ice‑cold 10 % glycerol, centrifuge again under the same conditions, discard supernatant, then resuspend in 30 mL ice‑cold 10 % glycerol and centrifuge a final time (4 000 × g, 15 min, 4 °C).

steps.title: Final glycerol wash and concentration
steps.instruction: Transfer the final pellet to a sterile 50 mL conical tube, add ice‑cold 10 % glycerol to bring the volume to 50 mL, and centrifuge at 4 000 × g, 15 min, 4 °C. While this spin runs, prepare a dry‑ice/ethanol bath (dry ice pellets covered with ethanol in a Styrofoam box). After the spin, discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in ~0.3 mL ice‑cold 10 % glycerol using a 1 000 µL pipette tip cut ~3 mm off the end.

steps.title: Measure cell density and adjust
steps.instruction: Measure OD₆₀₀ of the resuspended cells after making a 1:500 dilution (e.g., 998 µL water + 2 µL cells). Multiply the reading by 500; the desired OD₆₀₀ is 200–300. If >300, dilute with cold 10 % glycerol; if <200, repeat a centrifugation‑resuspension step with a smaller glycerol volume (e.g., 0.1 mL) and re‑measure.

steps.title: Aliquot and freeze competent cells
steps.instruction: Pipette 35 µL of the cell suspension into each 0.6 mL Eppendorf tube, place the tubes in the dry‑ice/ethanol bath rack so the bottom half of the tube is immersed but the cap stays above the ethanol, and freeze for ~2 min. Remove, wipe dry with a Kimwipe, and store the frozen tubes in a dry‑ice box, then transfer the box to a –80 °C freezer. Repeat until ~20–30 aliquots are prepared. After use, allow the bath to sublimate in a fume hood; ethanol can be collected for reuse, but keep the bottle loosely capped to vent CO₂.

steps.title: Prepare antibiotic LB agar plates for transformation
steps.instruction: Sterilize LB/agar, cool to touch, and pour 50 mL into a sterile 50 mL conical tube. Add 35 µL each of ampicillin (100 mg/mL), kanamycin (50 mg/mL) and spectinomycin (100 mg/mL) stock solutions to obtain final concentrations of 70 µg/mL Amp, 35 µg/mL Kan, and 70 µg/mL Spec. Mix and pour ~20–25 mL into each 100 mm plate. Let solidify with the lid slightly ajar for 30 min, label plates (e.g., “sfGFP‑WT” and “sfGFP‑150TAG”), and keep on ice.

steps.title: Set up electroporation mixes
steps.instruction: Pre‑chill two 1 mm electroporation cuvettes on ice for 15 min and two 0.6 mL Eppendorf tubes. For the WT tube, add 2 µL each of pRBC‑sfGFP‑WT, pERM2‑nhpSer, and pCDF‑Frb‑v1 plasmids (≈ 100–500 ng each). For the TAG tube, add 2 µL each of pRBC‑sfGFP‑150TAG, pERM2‑nhpSer, and pCDF‑Frb‑v1. Chill the tubes 5–10 min.

steps.title: Electroporate and recover cells
steps.instruction: Thaw electro‑competent BL21(DE3) ΔserC cells rapidly, keep on ice, and add 30 µL cells to each plasmid mix, gently pipetting 2–3 times. Transfer each mixture to a pre‑chilled cuvette, wipe electrodes dry, and electroporate at 1 500 V (1 mm cuvette) for a time constant of 4–6 ms. If arcing occurs, discard and repeat with a fresh mix diluted 1:1 with cold MQ water. Immediately add 1 mL SOC to the cuvette, transfer to a 1.7 mL tube, and recover at 37 °C, 250 rpm for 90 min. While recovering, wash cuvettes sequentially with MQ water, 0.1 M HCl, MQ water, and 70 % ethanol; dry upside‑down on a Kimwipe and store capped.

steps.title: Plate transformed cells
steps.instruction: After recovery, pellet each 1 mL culture at 3 000 × g for 3 min, discard ~900 µL supernatant, resuspend the pellet in the remaining ~100 µL, and spread evenly onto the corresponding antibiotic LB/agar plate. Let plates dry with lids partially open for ~20 min near a flame, then incubate upside‑down at 37 °C overnight (~16 h).

steps.title: Prepare starter cultures for expression
steps.instruction: In 14 mL sterile culture tubes, add 5 mL starter media (2× YT + 0.5 % v/v glycerol) containing 70 µg/mL Amp, 35 µg/mL Kan, and 70 µg/mL Spec. Scrape several dozen to hundreds of colonies from each transformation plate into the respective tube, break up the cell clumps by gentle pipetting, and grow at 37 °C, 250 rpm for 3–4 h until OD₆₀₀ > 1. Do not let cultures reach stationary phase.

steps.title: Prepare TB expression media
steps.instruction: For a 50 mL test expression, add 5 mL sterile 10× potassium phosphate buffer to 45 mL 1.1× TB in a 250 mL baffled flask; for a 1 L expression, add 100 mL 10× buffer to 900 mL 1.1× TB in a 2.8 L Fernbach flask. Add the same antibiotics as above and 1–2 drops (50 mL) or 5–6 drops (1 L) antifoam. Keep media at room temperature.

steps.title: Inoculate and grow expression cultures
steps.instruction: For 50 mL expressions, add 1 mL of the appropriate starter culture to 50 mL TB media (in a baffled 250 mL flask); for 1 L, add 10–20 mL starter to 1 L TB (in a 2.8 L flask). Grow at 37 °C, 200–250 rpm until OD₆₀₀ = 1.0 (≈ 3–5 h).

steps.title: Induce protein expression
steps.instruction: Add IPTG to a final concentration of 0.5 mM (50 µL of 0.5 M IPTG stock for 50 mL; 1 mL for 1 L). Reduce temperature to 30 °C for sfGFP‑WT (or 20–30 °C for other targets, never above 30 °C). Add additional antifoam (1–2 drops for 50 mL; 5–6 drops for 1 L). Continue shaking at 200–250 rpm for 20–24 h.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence and OD
steps.instruction: After 20–24 h induction, measure OD₆₀₀ and sfGFP fluorescence (ex 488 nm / em 510 nm). Dilute cultures 1:10–1:100 in PBS if needed (e.g., 100 µL culture + 1 900 µL PBS for a 1:20 dilution). Expected sfGFP‑150TAG fluorescence should be ~20–30 % of WT, corresponding to 50–150 mg L⁻¹ of protein.

steps.title: Harvest cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge cultures at 5 000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, and resuspend pellets in an appropriate buffer (e.g., 50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 500 mM NaCl, 10 % v/v glycerol, 5 mM imidazole for His₆‑tag purification). Add 10 % glycerol as a cryoprotectant if cells will be frozen. Cells may be flash‑frozen in liquid N₂ and stored at –80 °C or processed immediately.

steps.title: Validate incorporation by Phos‑tag gel
steps.instruction: Run SDS‑PAGE with Phos‑tag acrylamide (50 µM Phos‑tag, 100 µM MnCl₂, 29:1 acrylamide:bis) at 120 V for 1.5 h at room temperature. Do not include molecular‑weight markers (they contain EDTA). Load WT, pSer control, and nhpSer samples side‑by‑side. If no shift is observed, increase Phos‑tag concentration, reduce protein load, lower total acrylamide % (e.g., 10 % vs 15 %), and ensure sufficient gel length for separation.

steps.title: Confirm by mass spectrometry
steps.instruction: Perform whole‑protein high‑resolution MS to distinguish nhpSer (Δ = 1.98 Da) from pSer; if resolution is insufficient, use bottom‑up MS/MS after tryptic digest. Account for sfGFP chromophore maturation (loss of H₂O and 2 H⁺, 20 Da lower than the sequence mass).

steps.title: Optional western blot verification
steps.instruction: If desired, probe blots with phospho‑Ser antibodies (recognition of nhpSer is uncertain) or with tag‑specific antibodies (e.g., FLAG, MYC) that bind regardless of phosphorylation. Note that western blots cannot quantify incorporation without a fully phosphorylated standard.
